title: Platform command to a ground station
description:
One object per message on cmd/gsu/{station_id}. A command is a request, never a guarantee: the platform confirms nothing itself and waits to see the effect in the station's own telemetry. Every command below therefore has a field in a telemetry payload that reports its result - if you add a command, add that field too. Unknown commands must be ignored, not rejected: an older station and a newer platform have to coexist.

The leased commands (radio.audio, video.start) share one shape: the platform repeats the command while the demand exists, a repeat is a renewal rather than a second start, and the lease expiring is the stop signal. Silence has to be the off switch because most consumers never say goodbye - a closed laptop, a dropped link, a crashed platform - and every one of those must stop a station transmitting to nobody on a metered link.

freq_hz.description: Already snapped to the nearest kHz by the platform. Reported back as radio.freq_hz.

db.description: Fixed threshold. Setting one implies leaving AUTO, exactly as moving the slider does on a real receiver. Reported back as radio.threshold_db.

on.description: On: ride 8 dB above the measured floor. Off: FREEZE the threshold where it was - do not keep tracking, or the control appears to do nothing. Reported back as radio.auto_squelch.
Momentary squelch defeat - the MON button. Station-wide: there is one gate, so this pushes hiss to every listener. Expected to be held, never latched. Reported back as radio.monitor.

gain.description: Site configuration, set once. Prefer fixed: the tuner AGC desenses near strong transmitters badly enough that a stronger signal reads lower. Reported back as radio.gain.

ppm.description: Crystal correction, trimmed once at commissioning. Reported back as radio.ppm.

on.description: Somebody is looking at the spectrum display, or has stopped. Demand-driven and re-requested periodically rather than held open by a connection, so a console that crashes stops the traffic without saying goodbye - the full sweep is roughly 150 MB a day on a metered link, for a display that is open for minutes at commissioning. Reported back as radio.spectrum and radio.span_hz, present only while asked for.

oneOf.description: Somebody is listening: let audio flow up the link (squelch permitting) for lease_seconds. Repeated while any console holds the audio subscription; a repeat is a renewal. There is no stop command - the lease expiring is the stop signal - and local recording is never gated by this: a transmission nobody had a console open for is still written to disk. Reported back as audio frames on gsu/{station_id}/audio while the squelch is open.

on.description: Always true. False is deliberately not defined: an unsubscribe-style stop would leave a station transmitting forever when the stopper never arrives, so stopping is the lease's job alone.

lease_seconds.description: How long this request is good for. The station clamps it to sane bounds, so an absurd lease cannot pin the uplink open.

oneOf.description: The first viewer attached: start the live H.264 stream to the media WebSocket (transport.md) and keep it running for lease_seconds. Repeated while anyone is watching; treat a repeat as a renewal, never a second start - there is one camera, and a second encoder on it reads as broken hardware. If the lease expires unrenewed the station stops on its own, so a crashed platform or a dropped link cannot leave it paying for a picture nobody can see. Reported back in health.video.stream.

lease_seconds.description: How long this request is good for. The station clamps it to sane bounds.

oneOf.description: The last viewer left. A courtesy that ends the stream sooner than the lease would; the lease expiring remains the guarantee, so a station that never hears this still stops. Reported back in health.video.stream.

reason.description: For the station's log, so 'stopped by the platform' can say why.

oneOf.description: Apply site configuration. Defined so both sides agree on the shape, and currently never sent: the platform holds no site policy of its own, and the settings it does share with the station (position, elevation) must not be editable from two ends - see enrolment.md §7 for when this changes. The station applies what it recognises, persists, and reports back as health.config_version; it never assumes the platform saw the change take.

version.description: The configuration generation this payload represents, echoed back in health.config_version once applied.

config.description: The settings to merge. Keys the station does not know are ignored, not rejected: a newer platform must be able to talk to an older station.

on.description: Reported back as light.on once the hardware has actually done it.
